# decisions.md — D-numbered architectural decision log (most recent first)

## D1150 [ROUTINE] — How a menu closes: the live-opener × rule, per-tier close control, resize and scroll closes (2026-09-24)

**Decision (Bean).** Wave 3C U-9 + U-11 run as one pair (families M-36, M-34, M-35, M-40, M-47, M-27, M-10), signed off after a two-model council: build the design, add `closeRadius`, and close-on-scroll for mouse and trackpad only (a swipe on touch must never lose the menu).
**Built** (c36105939). FR-36-6's × rule is DEC-15's own wording: the drawer's × is left out at a tier only when the drawer is `non-modal`, `closeStyle` at that tier is the new `trigger` value, and the opener is live (its centre hit-tests to itself); render.php emits the rule scoped to `[data-sgs-nav-opener-live]`, `store.js` sets the flag before focus and clears it first in `runClose`. `closeStyle`, `closePlacement` (`same-slot` needs `modal`), `closeOffset` and `closeRadius` are tier objects edited through `ResponsiveOverride`. DEC-09: the burger carries `data-sgs-nav-collapse`; the drawer closes on a width change only if the opener is no longer live, and focus always lands on a live control. `closeOnScrollDistance` (DEC-02's one carve-out, which drops the scroll lock while set), `accordionExclusive` (ENG-02), `burgerMorph`/`Duration`/`Easing`, `itemMagnetStrength`.
**Standards.** A Fable audit against Spec 32 (clean) and Spec 35 (seven must-fixes: the `ResponsiveOverride` pairing, enum control shapes, Settings placement, element manifest, reset-to-unset, Effects panel mount), all fixed before commit. Eight stored drawer posts on sandybrown migrated to the tier object before the deploy (`migrate-stored-tier-scalars.py`).
**Verified live** on sandybrown (`reports/visual-diff/nav-drawer-2026-09-24.md`), each with a negative control. Residue: two-bar burger (U-6), icon swaps and indus-foods' 38px × recorded as divergences, hotkey and history-back outside the wave; axe with the drawer open and the editor round-trip owed.

## D1149 [ROUTINE] — Build Eye Care by hand to client-ready first; the finished site becomes the pipeline's answer key (2026-09-24)

**Decision (Bean).** Stop finishing the cloning pipeline before any client ships. Build the Eye Care site by hand from the Claude Design gap map (`sites/eye-care-ward-end/Ward End Eye Care - SGS Gap Handoff/`), closing each gap as a general framework feature, full scope including the lens configurator and prescription upload. Done = fully functional and matching the draft; client-supplied content is out of scope. Then clone the same draft onto a separate test page and compare rendered output against the finished site: every difference is a pipeline gap with a known destination.
**Sub-decisions.** Lens prices = one site-wide add-on price list, a second priced-step source in Spec 43 (not WC variations). Prescription upload reuses `sgs/form-field-file` + `class-form-upload.php`, gaining private storage (files currently land in the public uploads folder). Converter findings design C1/C3/C4/C5 paused (C2 shipped 0deb3b10b); they return as Phase 7 test cases.
**Checked.** Gap map mostly accurate; its theme row was stale (snapshot already Playfair/Outfit, ink/taupe) and it over-sized the configurator and upload (choice-flow Phases 1-2 and the uploader exist).
**Plan.** `plans/2026-09-24-eye-care-hand-build-design.md` (phases, parallel waves, model routing).

## D1148 [ROUTINE] — One shared scrim for every block that dims the page; one hover-shadow control (2026-09-24)

**Decision (Bean).** U-2 (M-14) signed off: colour or gradient plus per-device strength and blur, on the drawer and on the menu bar (so every dropdown and mega panel on a bar shares it); the bar is off unless set; lamalama's click-through is an accepted divergence (SGS absorbs the dismissing click). Widened by Bean: build it as a shared helper any dimming block adopts, so the modal (pop-up), cart drawer, gallery lightbox and product search adopt it too; the modal's backdrop hover colour is removed. Separately: blocks with a shadow get ONE hover-shadow control (the lift switch plus an optional chosen hover preset that overrides it), not two.
**Built.** `includes/helpers-scrim.php::sgs_scrim_render` (tint on `::before`, blur on the element, open state from CSS `:root:has(<open selector>)`, printed at `wp_footer`); `src/components/ScrimControls.js`; `supports.sgs.scrim` plus `scrimColour`, `scrimColourGradient`, `scrimOpacity`, `scrimBlur` on nav-drawer, nav-bar-menu, cart, gallery, modal, product-search, each keeping its old look as its default; detector `scripts/scrim/check-scrim.py` (fast gate); converter routing through a `scrim` manifest element and the new `fill/css:backdrop-filter` cluster member. Fixes a live double dim on part-width modal drawers. `src/components/ShadowLiftControls.js` holds the one hover-shadow control; `sgs_shadow_lift_enabled` lets a chosen preset win. Commits 4d445a7d2, 5cbee72ba.
**Council.** Sonnet code-path census and Haiku adversarial reader: GO WITH FIXES twice (design, then Addendum A); every fix applied (`.claude/reports/2026-09-24-u2-scrim-design.md`).
**Verified live** on sandybrown (`reports/visual-diff/scrim-2026-09-24.md`): the six scrims at their measured values, open, close, click-absorb and Escape. Also repaired five fast gates that failed on main for unrelated reasons (2aa9fcd64) and gave Mama's snapshot the shadow set and hover map (cc1f7a1b8).

## D1147 [ROUTINE] — Overlay content and nested loop items are reported, never converted into the page (2026-09-24)

**Decision (Bean, design approved).** On the Eye Care page, about 20 blocks of raw loop templates (`{{ o.title }}`) sat below the last section. There were two proven routes: content that shows only while a drawer, modal, cart or mega panel is open sits outside every screen, so it was treated as page content; and a `<sc-for>` item boundary inside another boundary was converted again as a standalone section.
**Built.**
- `orchestrator/screen_route.py::overlay_flags` / `overlay_of`: Stage 1 now calls `draft-manifest/manifest.py::build_manifest`, read-only, written to `draft-manifest.json`. An outside-screen boundary under an overlay's gate gets `screen_role="overlay"`, and Stage 4 reports it as `overlay-content` with the overlay entity (Spec 36 builds overlays as their own posts).
- `orchestrator/boundary_nesting.py::nested_item_owners`: an item inside another boundary is reported as `nested-item` with its owner. This is universal: static drafts have no items. Spec 44's recognition still runs first.
**Verified.**
- Tests: `tests/test_screen_route.py`, `tests/test_boundary_nesting.py`, with negative controls.
- Eye Care re-clone (run `2026-09-24-000044`, v2 draft): 14 overlay pieces and 1 nested item reported; the live page carries 0 `{{` at 1440, 768 and 375, and all real sections are present. The only other markup change is the D1145 full-width revert, now live.
- Mama's drafts carry no `<sc-for>` and no screens, so neither rule can fire there.
**Found.** The Eye Care snapshot is extracted from the v1 draft folder (classless), while clones use v2 (SGS-BEM). Clones therefore need `--skip-freshness-gate` until v2 extraction stops picking the reviews block's Google blue as primary.

## D1146 [ROUTINE] — Every shadow lifts on hover by default; each preset has its own hover partner (2026-09-24)

**Decision (Bean).** "Auto lift on hover should be default": everything with a shadow lifts, including non-clickable boxes, with a per-block switch to turn it off; each decorative preset gets its own matching hover rather than all becoming Floating. Rejected: a one-click button only (Bean chose the default), and a single procedural lift for presets (it cannot give each decorative style its own hover).
**Built.** `theme.json::settings.custom.shadowHover` (whisper to soft, soft to lifted, lifted to floating, floating higher; crisp, long, outline, grounded, glow, hard with matching literals; pressed unchanged); `includes/helpers-shadow-hover.php` (`sgs_shadow_hover_value`, `sgs_shadow_hover_rules`) with a JS twin and shared cases; dark variants of the hover literals; every PHP emitter, the wrapper, card properties, supports.shadow blocks and the media atom; `scripts/shadow-lift/` for stylesheets, run BEFORE the hover guard; `shadowLiftOnHover` on 21 blocks via `scripts/fanout-shadow-lift-attr.py`; overlays (mega-panel, nav-drawer, modal, cart) declare `supports.sgs.shadowLift: false`. No `transition` is added (a second `transition` shorthand cancels a block's own).
**Council.** Sonnet adversarial: GO WITH FIXES; both blockers (hover-guard ordering, transition shorthand) resolved in the design before the build.
**Verified live** on eye-care-test (`reports/visual-diff/container-2026-09-23.md`): preset lift on light and dark bands, switch-off negative control, Hard's own hover, a touch tap does not stick. Commits 9a309281a, 8b18b9d75.
**Also ruled (Bean, 2026-09-23).** Dark-surface shadows signed off by eye; mega-panel `borderRadius` stays a single value; buck's `auto` z-index accepted (the visual result is measured, not the code).

## D1145 [ROUTINE] — Content width is a per-site setting read by Spec 33, not a converter rule; reviews header matches at 12 widths; comparison method written down (2026-09-23)

**Bean's rulings.** "Don't keep the rule. The content and wide width values are supposed to be customisable per site, so the Spec 33 pipeline should pick this up and set it." The draft was designed for UX and CRO, so the clone must match it on every device width, not only 1440/375. The whole-site audit runs next, with screenshots at all three device widths, after a compact.

**Done.** Reverted the converter full-width rule (e4ccdeeb5, reverts 071d46fb6). FR-33-19 (e73c8a66b): the extractor measures every top-level row at 1440 and 1920 and writes `settings.layout.contentSize`/`wideSize`; Eye Care contentSize 1336px (hero, best sellers, "not sure what suits you", about strip), wideSize 1440px (why buy, reviews, optician). Reviews header (679db12b6): logo and rating are one group at natural width, the caption stacks over the score row, wrapped buttons start at the left (`space-between`); draft and live agree at all 12 widths from 360 to 1920. Comparison method + tools committed: `plugins/sgs-blocks/scripts/parity/draft-vs-live/README.md`, Spec 20 FR-20-12.

**Deploy note.** With Bean's go-ahead, eye-care-test was deployed with `--allow-dirty --skip-gate-full`: it carried another session's uncommitted edits (container wrapper, colour variants, shadow hover, several blocks), and the full gate tier failed only on an advisory ratchet from other blocks (rule 21, 6 vs 5).

**Open.** The converter must set `contentWidth: "wide"` on rows whose draft content uses the site's wide width (only visible above 1440); page 11 has not been re-cloned since the revert; other screens use 996/1200 widths; the draft decides phone/tablet from its content width (viewport minus scrollbar), so at exactly 768–783 in a desktop browser it shows its phone layout while the site shows tablet.

## D1144 [INCIDENT] — Reviews card reported "matching" when it was not; Google design becomes the baseline; four site-level causes fixed (2026-09-23)

**What went wrong.** D1142's "matches" compared only style values of text-matched elements at two widths; Bean found six failures by eye (heading indent, fonts, logo size/side, missing card logos, arrows over the cards, dots). Standing rule now: compare at 1440/768/375, check positions, presence and loaded fonts, then look at the side-by-side captures before reporting (memory `compare-draft-vs-live-at-all-three-device-widths`).

**Bean's rulings.** The Google design is the block's default look, with the other looks kept; five arrow placements, none may cover content; the navigation layer is shared (reviews first, the other two sliders later); layout choices are read from a draft's structure; the look detector keeps the default on a tie; containers with no drafted width are full width; every loaded-and-used font is captured; Google Fonts consent on by default and snapshot Google fonts self-hosted automatically; deploys must not overwrite a client's theme.

**Built.** Shared slider navigation (`includes/helpers-slider-nav.php`, `assets/css/slider-nav.css`), baseline defaults (2cd55dadf, b41c4ef0b, 5f98e9050); layout-choice rungs and prefer-default rule (59d6e0ef6, 567fda19e); full width on absence (071d46fb6, 811 containers across the corpus, Mama's included, Bean-approved); fonts (43da2aa9a); deploy ships the client theme.json and fails closed (8785b1179; sandybrown and indus-test were also serving framework files). Design: `.claude/plans/archive/2026-09-23-google-reviews-baseline-and-slider-nav-design.md`.

**Verified.** Eye Care page 11 at 1440 and 375 equals the draft on every structural check; fonts self-hosted. At 768 the draft uses its content width (viewport minus scrollbar), so it shows its phone layout; at 790 both match.

**Open.** Stars read slightly larger than the draft's text-glyph stars; testimonial-slider and trustpilot-reviews to adopt the shared navigation; `render.php`, `edit.js`, `assembly.py`, `manifest_annotation.py` over the file-length rule; the next theme deploy to sandybrown switches it to Mama's committed snapshot.

## D1143 [ROUTINE] — Wave 3C U-1 closed: nav surfaces de-hardcoded; universal shadow-tone check shipped alongside (2026-09-23)

**U-1 (`plans/2026-09-21-wave-3c-implementation-plan.md` §4).** Six commits de-hardcode the nav surfaces per the signed families. Commit 1 (mega close-grace): the mega interactivity context in `nav-menu-markup.php` reads `submenuCloseGrace` instead of a literal 170, so the operator-set close-grace attribute now reaches the mega panel, not only the dropdown. Commit 2: `contrastSafe`'s `force-solid` value paints the header's own resting `background` (`includes/sgs-header-force-solid.php`) instead of only suppressing transparency. Commits 3/3b: `sgs/site-header` gains a per-tier `zIndex` object (`includes/sgs-header-z-index.php`), and the drawer's non-modal z-index scale derives from it. Commit 5: `submenuIntentDelay` and `submenuOpenOn` (hover or click) give an operator-set intent delay and open mode on the dropdown and mega contexts.

**Surface ground (4a-4f).** `includes/helpers-surface-ground.php` (`sgs_surface_backdrop_decls`, `sgs_surface_fill_alpha`) is the one emitter behind `surfaceBlur`/`surfaceSaturate`/`surfaceOpacity` on `sgs/site-header`, `sgs/mega-panel`, `sgs/nav-drawer`, `sgs/container`, `sgs/cta-section`, `sgs/hero`, `sgs/multi-button`, `sgs/physics-canvas`, `sgs/site-footer` and `sgs/trust-bar`, with one Surface panel (`container/components/BackgroundPanel.js`) and one editor preview (`src/utils/surface-preview.js`). `sgs/site-header` also gains `surfaceFadeEdge` (none/top/bottom, off in forced-colours mode, commits d304e1185/6a0a8d76a). `sgs/mega-panel` and `sgs/nav-drawer` each gain a `shadow`/`shadowColour` writer (`sgs_shadow_box_decls`, commit 0980e8b1d for the drawer). 4f-1 shipped the layered shadow control and theme presets; 4f-2 (commit 96b1812bf) has the converter clone a multi-layer box-shadow as a shape list plus a colour list (`converter/services/shadow_layers.py`, `db_lookup.attr_for_shadow_colour_sibling`), converter council GO WITH FIXES (the sgs/media colour pairing fix applied).

**Item hover paint (commit a8e537dc6).** `sgs/nav-bar-menu` and `sgs/nav-drawer-menu` gain `itemOpacity`/`itemOpacityHover` (top-level item + caret) and `submenuOpacity`/`submenuOpacityHover` (the dropdown/mega/accordion sublink, a genuinely different value on some references) plus `itemPaddingShiftHover` (inline-start padding growth on hover); `sgs/mega-panel` gains `panelCardLift` (default 3px, the value hardcoded before this attribute existed) and its own `itemPaddingShiftHover`. Every rule goes through `sgs_hover_state_rules`; the sliding-pill hover (`itemBgHoverTreatment`) already applied to panel-less items with no change needed.

**Family coverage (`families-master.json`).** M-43 (panel open mode/intent delay/close grace) moves to `covered`; residual: rabbit's open state was never reproduced live. M-21 (item hover paint) moves to `covered`; its attributes are built and PHP-tested, and live verification of the card lift and the submenu opacity pair on a `qa-hdr-*` fixture is owed. M-09 (header stacking) moves to `covered`: buck's `auto` z-index is an accepted divergence (Bean). M-13 (surface ground) stays `partial`: the mega-panel `borderRadius` stays a single value (Bean), and the edge-fade's own live check is owed.

**Universal shadow-tone check (design `.claude/reports/2026-09-23-shadow-tone-design.md`, Bean-approved GO WITH FIXES applied).** A surface is judged dark when white text would be chosen for it (`helpers-colour-wcag.php::sgs_wcag_white_wins_for_luminance`); `helpers-surface-tone.php::sgs_surface_tone` judges overlay, image, gradient and colour layers; the wrapper, nav-drawer and mega-panel mark `sgs-on-dark`/`sgs-on-light`; `helpers-shadow-dark.php` gives a dark surface a black shadow at 2.2x plus a 1px light ring; the editor mirrors it in `src/utils/surface-tone.js` and `surface-preview.js::wrapperToneClass`; the default shadow colour follows `--wp--custom--shadow-colour`; stylesheet black shadows are migrated; `scripts/check-shadow-sources.py` gates colour reachability, undefined variables and style-engine forced-colours; forced-colours for stylesheets stays with `scripts/shadow-fallback/`. Commits 7dcedb346, c6d71ced8, c82ec0fb4, 298f7e45c, d53805634, 9759d039b, f9f20b8e7, ca5621aa6, 662b7235f, ba01058ee.

**Councils.** U-1 (Sonnet adversarial + Haiku verifier): GO. 4f-2 converter council: GO WITH FIXES. Shadow-tone design council: GO WITH FIXES.

**Live evidence.** `reports/visual-diff/container-2026-09-23.md`, `nav-drawer-2026-09-23.md`, `nav-bar-menu-2026-09-23.md`, `container-2026-09-21.md`, `mega-panel-2026-09-21.md`.

**Bean's rulings (2026-09-23).** The dark-surface shadows look right by eye on every band. `sgs/mega-panel::borderRadius` stays a single value (no per-device migration: no reference needs it). buck's `auto` z-index is accepted as a divergence: the visual result is what is measured, not the code. **Docs.** `.claude/LEDGER.md`, `plans/2026-09-21-wave-3c-implementation-plan.md`, `.claude/verify/merged-spec36-37-track.md`, Spec 36 (spec_version 2.7), Spec 37 (spec_version 1.4.0 — the `force-solid` FR-37-44 description corrected to match the shipped behaviour) and `families-master.json` all updated in the same pass. **Next: U-2**, surface scrim colour, alpha and blur per tier (M-14), design-gated, not started.

## D1142 [ROUTINE] — Selector-routed fold and the reviews block redesign: the Eye Care reviews card now matches the draft (2026-09-23)

**Bean's steer.** "The pipeline should be using whatever categorical data, code or info is available to it" (approved the selector-routed fold); the reviews block must replicate the draft's Google setup and offer ready-made looks, with the attributes that setup needs.

**Shared mechanism (converter, rule 7 approved).** A per-area declaration that `attr_for_area_property` misses is looked up again by the element's own class against each attribute's `derived_selector`, and the property against its `css_property` (`fold_helpers._selector_route_attr`, `db_lookup.attrs_for_element_class_property`). Guards from three cold council raters: only the class that IS the area routes; a class claimed by two block elements is reported, never guessed; an ambiguous first lookup is a skip row, not a crash; box attributes are written in their declared object shape; width/height route only for an attribute that lists them. Follow-ups found live: a padding box attr is found through the selector route (`padding` shorthand), and a one-side border shorthand expands for the per-area fold only (`per_side`) because on the root path it would paint a text-coloured line on blocks whose `borderStyle` defaults to solid. Seeder: `supports.sgs.presetManualValues` names looks chosen by hand, so detection never auto-picks them. Commits d160fe287, 859efac76, 75a4cfe57.

**Block.** `sgs/google-reviews` gains 240 attributes (77 named, 13 typography families), six Styles panels, and eight looks on `cardStyle`; "Write a review" defaults to an outlined button; text clamps at 8 lines. Commit ec1e28dd4; design `.claude/plans/archive/2026-09-21-google-reviews-block-design.md`; report `reports/visual-diff/google-reviews-2026-09-23.md`.

**Verified.** Live Eye Care page 11 at 1440 and 375 against the draft: both header buttons match size and colour by pixel sample, stars gold, card radius/padding/border, avatar, captions and Roboto match; review cards 6 to 8px taller. Real editor: all looks and display types render, no failed request. Corpus of 474 sections: Mama's identical throughout.

**Open.** Review cards slightly taller; the rail's 16px gap and star letter-spacing have no attribute; `render.php` (about 1,200 lines), `edit.js` (720) and `manifest_annotation.py` (about 2,100) exceed the file-length rule and need splitting; one-side borders on block ROOTS need their own design (colour has no all-sides home).

## D1141 [ROUTINE] — Editor crash and reviews canvas fixed; the whole reviews card becomes one block; ticker one slim row; council-reviewed twice (2026-09-21)

**Bean's steer.** Fix the reviews block editor (giant stars stand-in, slider crash, default slider); reuse existing controls, never reinvent; typography for the ticker via the shared helper; "review all our recognition methods" before patching the draft header; all 13 reviews are five-star; do the small cleanups (marquee, svg upload message).

**Editor (commits `0d7e68bad`, `03b92be45`, `6a101c2a8`).** Selecting an `sgs/google-reviews` slider or any `sgs/gallery` crashed because `ToolsPanel` was imported by its unprefixed name (undefined in this WordPress; only `__experimentalToolsPanel` exists); both now import from `src/components/primitives` and `survey-experimental-imports.js` fails on any direct import of an aliased primitive. The canvas is now the real block through ServerSideRender (one short notice above sample reviews; an editor-only notice when empty); the empty state needed the shared hover-effects filter to stop appending a style tag to empty output. Default variant is slider; the aggregate never prints 0.0. The trust-bar marquee with no breakpoint never started (its track shrank to the bar); fixed. A refused `.svg` upload is worded as an action.

**Recognition review (three investigators, no draft edit).** 21 methods inventoried; only five decide anything on the reviews card. Spec 44 never ran on it (classed section); Spec 45 is built but unwired and cannot see static header text; `averageRating`/`reviewCount`/`businessName` were seeded with roles no content path accepts; the render-source scan followed one require hop so the header attributes read as `child`. Nine spec/code contradictions were corrected in Specs 00, 31 and 44.

**Built (commits `5190a0a6e`, `1667bbe8a`).** Annotator: a box-owner climb puts the block root on the bordered card (first ancestor painting a real box the block declares), a header ladder maps rating, count and link by role and value shape, per-card star glyph runs become `rating`, style mustache markers give `avatarColour`. Converter: svg presentation lift (`iconBareSize` 15, `iconColour`, `iconStrokeWidth` 1.6) with the lifted attributes stripped from stored svgs; variant detection with an identity-matched declaration signal; container typography routed only where `block_selectors` names the primary text attribute (trust-bar, option-picker, timeline); review scalar roles and a `colour-background` role; per-class skip rows for CSS that reaches no attribute.

**Council, twice.** Four cold Opus raters reviewed each wave and every wave went "ship after fixes". Proved and fixed: the "only one element" typography fallback wrote a nav drawer's font-size to its close button and a quote's to its citation (now selector-authoritative only); the variant probe could destroy a correct `icon-bare`; a divider wrapper under-climbed and silently dropped the whole header; a star bar's aria-label bypassed the agreement guard; the business-name rung was dead on the live DB; dropped CSS on block-owned classes was silent. Mama's homepage output is byte-identical (9 of 9 sections, plus 20 real drafts with 0 differences).

**Live result (Eye Care test site, real browser).** Ticker: one 39px row at 1440, 15px accent stroke icons, 12.5px label, marquee at 375 only. Reviews: the whole bordered card is one `sgs/google-reviews` (averageRating 4.7, reviewCount 15, 13 reviews each rating 5 with a coloured initial), 0 broken images. Editor: sample and written slider and grid canvases, the no-data notice and the gallery all select cleanly.

**Not achieved, stated.** Reviews card is not faithful: gold stars (#FBBC04) render taupe and the "Write a review" pill renders black because the draft styles those elements inline and the per-area fold routes only by element name, not by an attribute's `derived_selector` (a shared-mechanism change, awaiting Bean's approval); six real block gaps have no attribute (review-card box, avatar size and radius, pill radius, aggregate typography, star size, divider colour); "See all reviews", the "Google Reviews" caption, the footnote and the scrollbar are absent (the block draws its own or has no attribute). Ticker at 768 keeps four messages on two rows (the draft shows two on one). `_NOT_BOX_IDENTITY` became an inclusion list because no DB column says "makes a box" (a `makes_box` column on property_suffixes would remove it). 21 slug-literal hits in `recogniser/` need a design decision.

## D1140 [ROUTINE] — Media sideload fixed, reviews routed to sgs/google-reviews, icon library, marquee lift, trust-bar controls; council-reviewed (2026-09-21)

**Bean's steer.** Root-cause the three open items (reviews routing, ticker fidelity, media errors and brand count) with parallel read-only investigators, then build the fixes grouped by shared files, then `/qc-council`. Bean also asked for raw SVGs to become reusable native icons, not client-only, with the pipeline able to see what the library already holds.

**Built (five commits, `717b9b8a5`..`82aa40188`).** (1) Media: Stage 4i resolved images against the run copy's parent (no `assets/`), so 192 errors and 32 dead `http://assets/...` images; it now uses the original draft folder, dedupes 192 slots to 16 files, takes the site from `SGS_DEPLOY_SITE`, writes uploaded url and id back into the deployed markup, and fails closed on a partial upload (`--allow-partial-media`, `--no-media-sideload`). (2) Reviews: the JS resolver leaves `data-src-field` markers (only for a draft with a manifest); the annotator maps fields by exact name, manifest `fieldMap` or a DB synonym through a narrow slot (`who` is now an alias of `attribution`), withholds the rest, strips markers on every path; the 13 Eye Care reviews are one `sgs/google-reviews` block. A seamless-marquee duplicate (32 doubled logos) collapses to 16 only on evidence. (3) Converter: `resolvers/marquee.py` lifts an infinite linear translateX animation (at least 20 percent travel, on the items' container) onto blocks' `marquee-*` roles; a type gate (`validate.write_type_violation`) rejects wrong-kind writes (the `"bgKenBurns":"none"` incident; the source fix removed a raw `animation` mapping from six boolean flags); an inline svg with no icon slug reaches `iconSvg` cleaned of draft classes; a decorative (aria-hidden) image is never lifted as a content image. (4) Icon library: `assets/icons/sgs-icons.json` beside Lucide, one shared svg allowlist, proposals keyed by path fingerprint (`icon-proposals.jsonl`, gitignored working state), `promote-icon.py`; fingerprints keep command case. (5) Trust-bar: icon-only badge style, stroke width, per-device item gap and padding, marquee below 768 or 1024 with custom duration; `max-content` and `fit-content()` survive the wrapper and box sanitisers.

## D1139 [ROUTINE] — Manifest routing built (annotation stage, class-section boundary, decision log); no invented reviews; converter band-padding collision fixed (2026-09-21)

(2) `recogniser/per-section-convention-voter.py::auto_detect_sections`: an element whose BEM root class names a `blocks.tier='class-section'` block is a boundary whatever its tag (DB-derived; the boundary lists of 39 drafts are unchanged). ## D1132 [ROUTINE] — Draft standardisation council: close the wiring gaps in existing code first; a small draft standard only for what code cannot derive; a deterministic second layer (2026-09-20)

**Bean's corrections that shaped it.** (1) The idea was NOT to rewrite a draft into Mama's shape or add a normalise stage: it was to move the README's facts into the draft files, so the pipeline reads them directly instead of extending code to read prose. (2) Do not limit the pipeline for other formats; add code only where it ignores information. (3) Claude Design writes the facts in AND a second layer checks them, because one AI pass misses things. Approved plan: `.claude/plans/2026-09-20-draft-standardisation-plan.md`.

**Findings (five-part council, real drafts and code).** The JS-to-CSS translation exists and is not wired: `orchestrator/script_bindings.py::resolve_tier_bindings` has no caller (padding 0px, one-column grids, 48 dropped declarations in run `eye-care-ward-end-eye-care-birmingham-2026-09-20-015848`); `--resolve-js-content` defaults off; the sc_var bridge flag is absent from the run command. The pipeline silently ignores `<sc-if>` conditions (95), `style-hover` (64), multi-field JS-array items (all the copy: PRODUCTS 16x21, REVIEWS 13, FAQS 8, REASONS 4, BRANDS 44), base64 `LOGOS`, and `data-reveal`/`data-rm`; `draft-manifest` is built and uncalled. The README holds only 12 to 15 facts no code reads and is wrong in 8 places against the files (Home order and two sections, nav, wordmark tracking, underline width, FAQ count, navy values, bag is a drawer), so the draft files are the source of truth.

**Decisions.** (1) Every gap is classified CODE, READ, SCHEMA/ASK or MEASURE by one test (in the plan, section 1b). (2) Track A wires and extends existing functions, no new stage: evaluator overlay after the `@media` fold, JS content default-on with all fields, and small readers for the ignored parts, one commit each. (3) Track B, Spec 46, requires only what code cannot derive: page kind, slug, parent; a class per section; collection intent; short behavioural rules; carried in one embedded JSON block. Written in full only after Claude Design follows the closing prompt (kill condition: ignores it twice). (4) Track C: a deterministic checker plus a "draft construct coverage" test so no draft part is silently ignored. (5) Track D (entity registry, creation, reference resolution) needs its own design gate. (6) A generated class per element was rejected (it needs a class to carry per-device values, which rule 1 and the residual scoping reject); the design uses a tier-map overlay at the converter's single inline-style reader.

**Measured (Phase 0).** Of the 75 names the evaluator resolves: 17 have no threshold inside a device tier, 37 have only the 760 threshold (snap-eligible under the 10px rule of D1129, an 8px band), 21 need the residual path (700 for 16, and 620, 1060, 1100, 1160, 1280 for 5). The evaluator's sweep floor (320) is a sweep artefact, not a draft threshold. Command: `resolve_tier_bindings` over `Eye Care Birmingham.dc.html`, grouping `intra_tier` runs by start width.

**Bean's answers (same day).** Keep the 10px rule AND normalise the draft platform's own stated breakpoints to ours: the draft names four (`mob` 760, `narrow` 1024, `wide` 1280, `lensStack` 700). Proposed mapping recorded in the plan (section 7 Q1): below-tablet declared breakpoints move to 768, 1024 already equals ours, 1280 stays a bounded visual breakpoint; awaiting his confirmation of the two edge cases (700 to 768, 1280 stays). The closing prompt also asks Claude Design to adopt 768/1024 and to use the attached logo file (the client's folder holds only four JPEG logo drafts). Base64 images decode deterministically to the exact embedded bytes; Eye Care's 40 logo data URIs are small thumbnails, so a hash-named sideload is a placeholder until real logo files arrive.

**First test result (same day).** Claude Design followed the closing prompt: manifest (9 pages, 6 overlays, 19 repeated groups, 16 rules, 3 open items), an `sgs-` class on every section (40), 760 and 700 changed to 768, logo file used, README cut from 20KB to 4KB. Checked against the original: all visible text identical (373 of 373 lines), all datasets identical, no base64. Three faults, fixed by me in the bundle rather than another round with the tool: it DELETED the 40 brand logos and their markup at 4 template sites (restored as files decoded byte-for-byte from the original), it rewrote the ticker fit rule and wrapping, and it changed padding on 3 Google buttons (all reverted). Only 2 of its 40 classes are real block names (`sgs-hero`, `sgs-google-reviews`); the rest are section labels, so I added a `sectionBlocks` map of proposed blocks (unconfirmed) and closed the manifest vocabularies. Render check, original against patched at 375, 768 and 1440: text identical, no broken images, identical page height, one differing region (the 44 by 22 pixel header logo, intended). Only the Home screen was rendered. Process lesson (Bean): one prompt and one export, then the pipeline owner patches residue; no second round with the design tool. The prompt file is now that single prompt. Patched bundle: `sites/eye-care-ward-end/design_handoff_ward_end_eye_care_v2` (raw export kept beside it as `..._v2_raw`); both untracked.

**A1 built and verified (same day).** Commit `faaf79f0d`: the width evaluator is wired in (Stage -1.4), flags found by what the script reads, Bean's breakpoint rule in `breakpoint_snap.py`, values applied at the converter's single inline-style reader after the `@media` fold. Proven: 953 tests, Mama's byte-identical in place, Eye Care v2 dropped-binding gaps 44 to 11 and padding settings 38 to 54, live test page 11 padding and grid columns equal the draft and Bean's online copy at 375, 768 and 1440 for every section present, inline-styling audit 0 violations. Two things found on the way: (1) the evaluator failed 2 of 10 runs under heavy CPU load (its 20 s deadline; reproduced, budgets widened, one retry, still fails closed under extreme load); (2) a first live measurement showed padding 0 at 768 and missing sections at 375, which was a stale cached copy of the page (the site caches phone and tablet variants separately), not a defect; the re-measure after the cache refreshed is the result. Also measured: the existing JS-array resolver (`--resolve-js-content`, off by default) clears 1 of 33 remaining binding names (the ticker's), because it handles single-text-field items only; the rest are multi-field loop items, the saved site-settings map (`gmbHref` and the phone and social links, never read while converting) and one state-driven name. **Built** (commits 245e6a07e, 1fa7fb583, 526784068; live reports in `reports/visual-diff/site-header-pill-2026-09-20.md`): `sgs/site-header` `headerFloat` (per-tier tri-state), `headerFloatInset` (tier-of-boxes, default 1rem), `headerFloatCollapse` (one toggle plus a breakpoint, off by default), `backdropBlur`; Float > Sticky > Transparent through the one merged writer; hide-on-scroll travels `calc(-100% - inset)`; a mega panel matches the pill and plain dropdowns clamp inside it (`panel-bounds.js`). That value moves with scroll position, hide-on-scroll and any element above the header, so it would have changed today's number; the build publishes the pinned `top` offset plus the header height instead (identical for every `top:0` header in every scroll state, and clamped as a sum). **QC council** (two code reviewers, live verification twice) fixed: the shadow suppression under float and transparent (keyed on raw transparency, ignoring force-solid and direction), inputs that could emit invalid CSS, blur only applying with float, reset controls writing non-default values, the mega panel's max-height, a stale prose claim, and an inspector scan finding that the block-root component location hid the controls. With no float or blur set the emitted CSS is byte-identical for 143 header scenarios.

**Still open.** A force-solid tier keeps a transparent background (reproduced with float removed entirely, so it is not from the pill): the transparent merge has no honest off value for the header's own resting background. Every existing header's uid changed once because three defaulted attributes joined the hash (cache-file churn only, computed values identical). The pill's `maxWidth` must be the tier object the editor writes; a scalar string emits nothing (existing schema behaviour). Payment icons and the collapse modes are closed (D1127).

## D1129 [ROUTINE] — Script-binding wiring on hold; breakpoints within about 10px round to the device tiers (2026-09-20)

**Decisions (Bean).** (1) Do NOT wire the script-binding evaluator into the pipeline yet: Bean has an idea, to be raised after this session is compacted, that could change the design. (2) A draft width threshold within about 10px of a device-tier edge is ROUNDED to that edge (760 to the 767/768 edge, 1010 to the 1023/1024 edge, and so on). (3) A threshold further out than that follows the rule that already exists: the responsive value is written into the Additional CSS control (`sgsCustomCss`) of the block the element becomes.

**What this changes.** Spec 31 FR-31-5.2 (F-ii, an earlier Bean lock) says a non-device threshold is "never snapped, never dropped" and is captured as a `ResidualBand` in `sgsCustomCss`. The 10px window is an amendment to "never snap". It is NOT implemented, so FR-31-5.2 still describes today's behaviour; amend it when built. "About 10px" is Bean's approximation: confirm the exact tolerance before building. It should apply to both `@media` thresholds and the width flags read from a draft's script (`orchestrator/script_bindings.py`).

**Open for whoever builds it.** `_residual_selector_for` scopes a residual by the element's own SGS-BEM class, which a classless element does not have; the `&selector` convention inside the owning block's `sgsCustomCss` is the likely route. Where the element is not a block of its own (an inner band merged into a container), which block owns the rule is undecided.

## D1125 [ROUTINE] — Four open defects from D1122 fixed (three code fixes, one help line); two items remain open (2026-09-20)

**Fixed, each proved before the change and checked live on the canary** (`reports/visual-diff/nav-drawer-2026-09-20.md`, `reports/visual-diff/site-header-2026-09-20.md`): (1) A non-modal drawer opened from a trigger inside page content left `main` fully live. (2) The shrunk-header padding rule had an empty off value, so a tier with shrink off kept the wider tier's reduced padding; it now restores the resting padding (`padding-block:revert` would have reset to the browser default, so it was not used). (4) The scrolled-shadow control says it replaces the resting and hover shadow while scrolled.

The honest off value is the header's own resting background (a colour, gradient or image), so it needs a design decision. (b) The trigger-anchored drawer overhangs the left edge when its trigger sits near the right edge of the page (panel left edge = trigger right edge minus panel width: 44 - 420 = -376 on page 3699, against +55 for the header burger). Spec 36 defines no viewport clamp for the trigger anchor, so a clamp needs a spec amendment first; the mechanism is `nav-drawer/render.php::$sgs_nd_geometry_for_anchor` and `store.js::openDrawerFor`. ## D1123 [ROUTINE] — Draft manifest: screens, entities, references and build order, read-only (2026-09-20)

**Decisions (Bean).** The full-site cloner must know how many pages a draft holds. Blank-canvas pages clone normally; template-tied parts (shop, product, cart, checkout, order-received), the header, footer, menus and drawers, and modals get their own runs. The size guide is its own `sgs_modal`. The bag drawer is `sgs/cart` with `displayMode` drawer. The shop's filter drawer is a variant of the shop archive's filter (Spec 30 FR-30-3), not an overlay. Referable things must be built in an order that lets later content link to them, and a later reference to something already built must be recognised.

**Decisions (mine, on the evidence).** (1) Page shells come first in the build order, ahead of modals, menus and the header, because those carry links to pages and an empty shell costs nothing. (2) The Lenses screen is a choice flow, not a normal page, because the README's routes table describes it as the lens configurator; the draft also opens the same configurator as an overlay, so both point at one entity. (3) A region inside a screen is a state of that screen, not an entity.

**Verified.** Eye Care Birmingham: 9 screens, 4 normal pages, 6 entities, the size guide referenced from Product, Help and the footer. Mama's homepage: 1 page, no entities. Two faults in my first output were found by reading it, not by a test: every page appeared to link to Checkout and Order confirmed (a helper definition ran on into the next statement), and the mega menu was merged into the lens flow (its opener is named `openMegaLenses`). Both are fixed and covered by tests.

**Open.** Nothing consumes the manifest. Next: the per-client entity registry and its recognition step, then Home-screen-only cloning with classless sections admitted as containers (Spec 44 §11 A and B). The size-guide modal, bag drawer and filter drawer mappings rest on Bean's statements and the specs; whether Spec 30's built shop archive covers all ten filter groups is unchecked.

## D1120 [ROUTINE] — Spec 33 now reads a Claude Design draft's declared design system; per-site palette overlay; QC council fixes (2026-09-20)

**Decisions (Bean, this session).** (1) Spec 33 saves global defaults and settings only, never per-element values. (2) The site palette is an OVERLAY on the base SGS palette, generated once per site from the whole draft, holding only colours with a proven consistent role; drifting, one-off and third-party-widget colours stay literal hex on the blocks that use them; a README role called faint or placeholder gets no slot; real content that a draft coloured with its placeholder grey is treated as a real role. (3) The alternative accent sets (taupe chosen, sage and navy kept) are saved under `settings.custom.accentSets`, not as picker swatches. (4) Colours are counted from three sources: inline HTML, JS values that flow into a style attribute (product and reviewer colours are content, not styling), and the rendered page. (5) Static drafts must not change.

**Decisions (mine, on the evidence).** The README maps to base slugs by a role-word table held as data; `primary` and `primary-text` come from the measured primary button, and `surface` and `text` are checked against the rendered body (the rendered value wins). A declared colour is validated per row by usage in that row's allowed families (one use is enough, a status colour has few); an undeclared colour needs 25 uses with 90% in one family. Where the phrase table has no answer, usage rank proposes an ADVISORY entry, never a firm one. The script's accent values beat the README's (Eye Care's navy differs; the script is what renders). FR-33-14 Tier 1 now includes an address or hours that a draft declares in a data object or beside an explicit label; free-text guesses stay Tier 2. Phone is stored in display form and `Sgs_Site_Info_Binding::prefix_url_for_key` strips it for the `tel:` link. A Claude Design draft gets a second freshness key, `draft_source_sha256`; static drafts keep the first only. Two Indus mega-menu drafts (no `:root` palette) change on purpose: Pass B no longer builds a one-colour palette from `::selection`, and their classless buttons are measured.

**Verified.** Mama's Munches and Indus: snapshot and trace byte-identical before and after for every draft that declares `:root` tokens (9 drafts: 6 Mama's Munches, 3 Indus; live hover values differ by the same noise two runs of the old code show); converter suite 863 passed. Eye Care test site: live `theme.json` equals the repo snapshot (0 differences); all 22 palette custom properties equal the snapshot at 1440px and 375px; no element paints the framework's teal or amber; Outfit `100 900` and Playfair Display `500 700` load and the H1 renders in Playfair Display at weight 500; `sgs_site_info` holds 13 settings; the Mama's and Indus test sites' `theme.json` are unchanged in content (identical to the framework file). Tests: 344 across the extractor, push, business-details and freshness-gate suites, each new fix proved by a test that fails without it.

**Review and council findings, all fixed.** Base slugs would have been deleted at push (the committed Eye Care snapshot had advisory entries with no saved base colour); a sample applicant's details in an application form were read as the business's; a Claude Design draft with a variant set but an unreadable README switched Pass B off and kept the framework teal; README tables whose value column was not named `Value` were dropped silently, and neutral role wording placed 3 of 10 colours; the freshness key could not see inline or script changes; the accent set was discarded when its inner keys differed; the committed Outfit file was Google's latin-ext subset, Playfair fell back to a single weight, and the draft's multi-word font link never matched; the measure step crashed on a Windows console; a failed server read looked like a fresh site; the snapshot push could not authenticate to a non-canary site.

**Open (none is Spec 33 scope).** The pipeline does not yet insert the saved values in place of `{{ }}` bindings: the map is written to `sites/eye-care-ward-end/site-info-placeholder-map.json` and nothing consumes it (Spec 31 runtime-binding stage, next). The cloned test page paints its template buttons transparent (26 measured, including one carrying `colourBackground` `#141414`), shows 59 distinct raw placeholders, and has no header or footer showing the saved details (`sgs_active_header` and `sgs_active_footer` are off). The primary button's hover text keeps the framework value. `test_site_info_binding.php` has 11 failures that exist at HEAD (operator-hint tests missing stubs). `measure.js` (332 lines) and `extract.py` (over 700) exceed the file-length guide. Files under `sites/eye-care-ward-end/` still untracked and not committed: the 3 MB offline copy of the draft, `sc-var-hints.json`, `uploads/`, `CLAUDE.md`. `push-theme-snapshot.py --snapshot-ssh-host` defaults to the canary's login.

## D1119 [ROUTINE] — Drawer looks are pattern data, seeded as posts; picker applies only the settings a look owns; QC council fixes (2026-09-19/20)

**Decisions (Bean, this session).** (1) The seven drawer looks are block patterns (`theme/sgs-theme/patterns/drawer-*.php`, keyword `featured`), not block variations; `nav-drawer`'s `variantPreset` and its seven variations are removed (zero stored uses on the canary, `indus-test`, `eye-care-test`). (2) Every `sgs_drawer` pattern except the blank starter is seeded as a published, non-Active Menu drawer post marked `_sgs_starter_slug`; only the drawer has a library (header and footer: no). (3) `featured` is a plain manual keyword: no scoring or coverage script (Bean: keep it generic, not worth the time). (4) The sidebar picker lists the `featured` looks and applies in one Undo step, changing only the settings a look owns (the attributes any look writes explicitly); "Keep my blocks" leaves the client's blocks untouched. (5) Seeded looks hold only blocks that render real site data. (6) The doc rule about decision numbers is: strip them where redundant or inside change/correction notes; a plain pointer to where a rule lives stays.

**Mechanics.** `Sgs_Starter_Library_Migration` runs on `init` and seeds when the signature (plugin version + registered library pattern slugs) differs from the stored one; a once-per-version gate seeded too early when the plugin was uploaded before the theme. A look in the bin counts as seeded until the bin is emptied. `registry.batch` hides a multi-dispatch apply from Undo; the working pattern marks each dispatch not-persistent and the last persistent. Spec 35 is split into 35 and 35A (parent + sub-spec, 1,392 + 1,024 lines).

**QC council result.** Five raters (live behaviour, code paths, docs, hygiene, adversarial design) found and this session fixed: Undo broken after applying a look; "Keep my content" overwriting client settings; placeholder copy in published looks; duplicate variations; numeric `"level":3` on `sgs/heading` (rendered `h2`) in four mega patterns, two footer templates and mega-group; `seed-starter <slug>` marker and error changes; container borders with no `borderStyle` (search, single, pricing); five false skip-log rows; stale LEDGER/Spec 19/37/35A text; a dead-domain URL in a gate. `check-dead-pattern-attrs.py` now fails on a type/enum violation and on a border width or colour without a style.

**Open.** Formal Gate 2 harness re-run; W2-u; W2-b create-inline; `build-deploy.py` does not purge Hostinger's CDN (use the Hostinger MCP `hosting_clearWebsiteCacheV1`); `setting-types.json` and `attr-role-map.json` still name `variantPreset` until regenerated (`attr-role-map.json` is dirty from another session); six `db-consistency` tests fail on schema/rename drift unrelated to this work; Specs 41 and 37 exceed the 1,500-line cap.

## D1116 [ROUTINE] — Stage 11.6 now scores the RENDERED draft (served over HTTP) for `.dc.html` drafts; honest baseline is content 12% / css 0%

**2026-09-19.** Investigator report `.claude/reports/2026-09-19-inv-stage116-draft-side.md`. Root cause
(PROVEN, and I re-ran it): Stage -2 swaps `args.mockup` into `run_dir/dc-import-resolved.html`, and
Stage 11.6 passed that file to `computed-parity.js` as `--draft` over `file://`. The run directory has no
`support.js`, so the draft was scored as raw template (176 unfilled `{{ }}`, 43 `<sc-for>`, 127 `<sc-if>`).
Same wrong-directory class as D1112. Mama's Munches was unaffected (its `args.mockup` stays the static file).

`<sc-for|if>` by CONTENT; `serve_dir` is an ephemeral-port `ThreadingHTTPServer` always shut down in
`finally`). The orchestrator captures `_draft_path` and `_is_dsl_draft` at Stage -2 and, for a DSL draft,
passes `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<original name>` to Stage 11.6, serving the ORIGINAL draft folder.
Static drafts keep the file path, unchanged. 3 new tests (14 pass with the resolver tests).

**Evidence.** Full deploy run after the fix printed `[stage-11.6] computed-parity (draft=Eye Care
Birmingham.dc.html [served over http] ...)` with content 12% / 11% / 12% and css 0% at 375/768/1440,
identical to the investigator's manual-server run. Both positive controls (served draft vs itself, clone
vs itself) score 100%, so the tool is sound. Over HTTP the draft shows ONE routed view (home, ~880
elements); ~11% (header, footer, announcement bar) legitimately is not in a homepage clone.

**Consequence.** The old "content 37% / css 4%" was inflated by placeholder-to-placeholder matches. 12% /
0% is the honest baseline for every later fix on this draft. Open: I did not audit other consumers of
`args.mockup` after the Stage -2 reassign for the D1112 class (only Stage -1.5 and 11.6 are fixed).
